text:
alex: RFC follow-up — hierarchical allocator rebalance (post-RFC notes). TL;DR: propose tenant-local buckets + a bounded cross-tenant steal path. Need to resolve offload ordering, fragment accounting, and paging backpressure.

sam: quick q — when you say 'bounded' steal path, what bounds are we comfortable with? time? pages moved? fairness windows? :thinking:

alex: bounds = twofold: (1) max-pages-per-rebalance-cycle (configurable, default 8), (2) per-tenant steal-rate limit (tokens/sec) to avoid noisy neighbor storms. goal is predictable latency.

priya: agree on rate limits. also we should gate cross-tenant steals behind residency delta > X to avoid thrashing (i.e., only steal if donor hotset drop > threshold).

maria: question on offload ordering: if we evict to host vs NVMe, do we prefer compactness-first (coalesce then offload) or latency-first (offload asap)?

alex: tradeoffs: compactness-first reduces fragmentation and long-term pressure, but increases short-term CPU/IO; latency-first keeps GPU quickly free for immediate work but may increase fragmentation and future compactions. propose policy enum: "LATENCY_PRI" | "COMPACT_PRI" with autoswitch heuristics based on free-rate.

jin: for paging/backpressure, can we leverage existing per-request admission hooks? e.g., if offload backlog > 200ms, reject large-batch requests with 429 or route to smaller shard?

priya: yes, we have hooks in request router. need clear SLA mapping: what backlog maps to which response? ops wants token-level attribution for rejections so we can notify customers.

alex: implementation note: allocator will expose a slim API:
```
// try_reserve(tenant, size) -> handle | E_RETRY | E_OOM
// release(handle)
 // steal_cycle() -> list<eviction_candidates>
```
Keep it minimal. stealing returns metadata only; runtime decides synchronous offload.

sam: can we include a cheap fragmentation score in candidate metadata (hotness, frag_ratio, contiguous_runs)? that helps runtime pick compactible victims before scattering small pages.

maria: +1. telemetry needed: histogram of frag_ratio pre/post rebalance, offload latency P50/P95, steal_rate. ops also wants a plan for rolling deploys (can we run old+new allocator simultaneously?).

alex: rolling deploys: allocator is feature-flagged. new nodes opt-in. cross-version interactions: if older node doesn't advertise steal API, newer nodes must avoid pulling from it. we'll include capability bit in node hello.

jin: concerning accounting: when we offload a page, which subsystem owns the bytes for billing? tenant or host? (we bill for host NVMe + egress)

priya: billing model: tenant billed for NVMe bytes and egress while page is pinned to its namespace. If page is demoted to shared hot cache (unattributed), we bill as system maintenance — but prefer to keep attribution to tenant where possible. ops to confirm with finance.

sam: edge-case: small allocations (subpage) and compaction. If compaction consolidates many tiny allocations into one large run, how do we handle pin handles and kv-cache?

alex: plan: compaction produces a rewrite token. runtime coordinates kv-cache migration: preview step to create new mapping, then atomic swap, then release old handles. will add safe-fallback: keep old mapping for N seconds before GC to tolerate races.

maria: can we add a short config snippet to the RFC repo? Ops wants knobs: steal_pages_per_cycle, steal_token_rate, frag_thresholds, offload_policy, compaction_grace_sec.

alex: sure — I'll push a draft. Also two TODOs: (1) simulation harness to run mixed workloads (large chat vs embedding) to validate steal knobs; (2) a small perf test that measures tail latency under background compaction.

jin: infra-bot: perf prod cluster can run a canary if you tag it with `allocator-canary-v1`.

alex: ack — I'll create canary config after draft. last note: want quick dev sync tomorrow 11a to agree on defaults. who can make it?

priya: I'm in.

sam: yes.

maria: can do.

alex: thanks all — I'll drop the draft RFC link and the config snippet in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
